# Data & hooks

The backend interface, the in-memory backend, and the hooks that load and save contest data.

### ContestProvider

Gives the data hooks their backend. Contest components themselves never read it: they take props.

```ts
import { ContestProvider } from '@/contest/context/ContestContext'
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `adapter` *(required)* | `ContestAdapter` |  | The backend: `createMemoryAdapter(seed)` for demos, your own implementation in production. |
| `children` *(required)* | `ReactNode` |  | The app. |

```tsx
const adapter = createMemoryAdapter(seed)

<ContestProvider adapter={adapter}>
  <App />
</ContestProvider>
```

- `useContestAdapter()` returns the adapter and throws a clear error outside the provider.

### ContestAdapter

Everything a contest app needs from a backend, as one typed interface. A real backend implements it; the in-memory adapter is the one that ships.

```ts
import type { ContestAdapter } from '@/contest/data/adapter'
```

```tsx
const adapter: ContestAdapter = {
  listQuestions: () => fetch('/api/questions').then((r) => r.json()),
  // …every other method of the interface
}
```

- Each write takes an optional `actor`: the name written into the audit trail.
- `revert(auditId)` puts an entity back the way it was before an entry. Only entries that kept a `before` snapshot can be reverted.
- `sendAnnouncement` fills the merge fields for each recipient, writes the in-app notifications and records how many people each channel reached (`Announcement.delivery`).
- `inviteParticipants` adds people as "invited" and skips an e-mail address that is already in the contest.

### createMemoryAdapter

A ContestAdapter that keeps everything in memory and in localStorage. It behaves like a backend: calls are asynchronous, writes leave an audit trail, submissions are scored from the answer keys, and uploads report progress and can fail.

```ts
import { createMemoryAdapter } from '@/contest/data/memoryAdapter'
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `seed` *(required)* | `ContestState` |  | The starting data. |
| `storageKey` | `string \| null` | `'contest.state'` | localStorage key for the saved state. `null` keeps it in memory only. |
| `latencyMs` | `number` | `120` | Pretend network delay for every call. |
| `uploadFailureRate` | `number` | `0` | Share of uploads (0 to 1) that fail at the end, to see the error and retry states. |
| `actor` | `string` | `'Admin'` | Name written into the audit trail when a call does not pass one. |

```tsx
const adapter = createMemoryAdapter(seed, { latencyMs: 200, uploadFailureRate: 0.2 })
adapter.reset() // back to the seed
```

- Returned objects are copies, so changing one never changes the stored state.
- `reset()` and `setUploadFailureRate(rate)` exist for demos and tests.
- There is no timer: a scheduled announcement that is due is sent the next time announcements or notifications are read. A real backend would use a job.
- Push reaches nobody who is still "invited" (no device yet), which gives the delivery report something to show.
- A submission becomes "reviewed" when no answer is left waiting for a person.

### useResource

Loads one thing and keeps it in state, with `loading`, `error`, `reload` and `mutate`. The small base the other contest hooks are built on.

```ts
import { useResource } from '@/contest/hooks/useResource'
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `load` *(required)* | `() => Promise<T>` |  | Fetches the value. |
| `deps` | `unknown[]` | `[]` | Loads again when one of these changes. |
| `options` | `{ pollMs?: number }` | `{}` | With `pollMs` it asks again every that many milliseconds, for news that arrives from elsewhere. |

```tsx
const { data, loading, error, mutate } = useResource(() => api.listQuestions())
await mutate(() => api.deleteQuestion(id)) // runs the change, then reloads
```

- `reload` keeps the old data on screen while it loads. `mutate` rejects with the original error so the caller can show it next to its form.

### usePacks

The topics and every pack, with `publish`, `restore` and `saveTopic`. Each write loads the snapshot again and rejects with a sentence when it is not allowed.

```ts
import { usePacks } from '@/contest/hooks/useContestData'
```

```tsx
const { data, publish, restore, saveTopic } = usePacks()
await publish({ topics: ['science', 'geography'], note: 'The new geography questions.' }, 'Ada')
await restore('pack-r3', 'The new pack had a problem.', 'Ada')
```

- The server builds the pack from the approved questions: `publish` only chooses topics. It refuses an archived topic, a topic with no approved question, a note that is too short and a pack equal to the one in force.

### useGate

The version gate in force, the one that starts later (if any), and how many players use each build, with `save`. Saving sends a new revision; the server keeps the list of builds the store offers.

```ts
import { useGate } from '@/contest/hooks/useContestData'
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pollMs` | `number` | `0` | Ask again every this many milliseconds. 0 means once. |

```tsx
const { data, save } = useGate(4000)
const rule = gateInForce(data.current, data.next, Date.now())
await save({ ...draft, message: 'Please update.' }, { confirmed: true }, 'Ada')
```

- `save` rejects with a sentence when the gate is not allowed: a minimum above the newest build, a link that is not https, a change that needs a confirmation.

### useModeration

The reports, the violations and who is working on which case, with `claim`, `release` and `resolve`. Every write loads the snapshot again.

```ts
import { useModeration } from '@/contest/hooks/useContestData'
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pollMs` | `number` | `0` | Ask again every this many milliseconds. 0 means once. |

```tsx
const { data, claim, release, resolve } = useModeration()
await claim('player:p7', 'Ada')
const { resolved, violation } = await resolve('player:p7', { action: 'suspend', days: 3, note: 'Answers within a second.' }, 'Ada')
```

- `resolve` rejects with a sentence when the decision is not allowed: someone else holds the case, the reason is too short, the question is in a show that has not finished. Show it in a toast.

### useQuestions

The questions, with `save`, `remove` and `review`. Needs a ContestProvider.

```ts
import { useQuestions } from '@/contest/hooks/useContestData'
```

```tsx
const { data: questions = [], save, remove, review } = useQuestions()
await save({ ...question, points: 20 }, 'Ada')
const { changed, skipped } = await review(['q34', 'q35'], 'preapprove', undefined, 'Ada')
```

- `review` does a review action (see `reviewActions`) to many questions. It resolves with what changed and what was left out, each with a reason; only a failure of the call itself rejects.

### useAnswerKeys

The answer keys of the given questions, by question id, with `save`.

```ts
import { useAnswerKeys } from '@/contest/hooks/useContestData'
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `questionIds` *(required)* | `string[]` |  | Which keys to load. They load again when the list changes. |

```tsx
const { data: keys = {}, save } = useAnswerKeys(questions.map((q) => q.id))
await save('q1', key, 'Ada')
```

### useMedia

The media library, with `upload`, `update` and `remove`. `upload` takes the same options as `MediaUploader` passes, so progress and cancel just work.

```ts
import { useMedia } from '@/contest/hooks/useContestData'
```

```tsx
const { data: assets = [], upload, update, remove } = useMedia()
<MediaUploader onUpload={(file, o) => upload(file, o)} />
```

### useProgram

The weekly program, with `save`. Saving sends a new revision; the server decides the revision number and refuses a change to a show that is on air, or a change to a show people registered for unless `confirmed` is true.

```ts
import { useProgram } from '@/contest/hooks/useContestData'
```

```tsx
const { data: program, save } = useProgram()
await save(draft, { confirmed: true })
```

- `save` rejects with a sentence a person can read: show it in a toast. See `impactOf` and `programChecks` for the same rules without a server.

### useRegistrations

How many people registered for each show, by occurrence key (`slotId@YYYY-MM-DD`).

```ts
import { useRegistrations } from '@/contest/hooks/useContestData'
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pollMs` | `number` | `0` | Ask again every this many milliseconds. 0 means once. |

```tsx
const { data: registrations = {} } = useRegistrations(5000)
registrations[occurrenceKey(slot.id, '2026-11-03')] // 864
```

### useEpisodes

The weekly shows, with `save`. Reading them is also what sends reminders that are due.

```ts
import { useEpisodes } from '@/contest/hooks/useContestData'
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pollMs` | `number` | `0` | Ask again every this many milliseconds. 0 means once. |

```tsx
const { data: episodes = [], save } = useEpisodes(5000)
```

### useLive

The live show now, or null. It asks again every few hundred milliseconds and the adapter works the state up to the server clock each time. `send` sends a command.

```ts
import { useLive } from '@/contest/hooks/useContestData'
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pollMs` | `number` | `400` | Ask again every this many milliseconds. |

```tsx
const { data: live, send } = useLive()
await send({ type: 'start' })
```

### useLiveShow

Everything a screen needs to show the live show: its state, the context the state machine needs, a `send` for commands, and the server clock.

```ts
import { useLiveShow } from '@/contest/hooks/useLiveShow'
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pollMs` | `number` | `400` | Ask again every this many milliseconds. |

```tsx
const { live, ctx, send, now } = useLiveShow()
if (live && ctx) return <LiveStage state={live} ctx={ctx} now={now} … />
```

### useLiveSimulation

Pretend players for a demo: bots join the lobby one by one and answer each question after a think time that depends on the bot and the question. A fixed seed gives the same crowd every time.

```ts
import { useLiveSimulation } from '@/contest/hooks/useLiveSimulation'
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `live` *(required)* | `LiveState \| null` |  | The live show now. |
| `ctx` *(required)* | `LiveContext \| null` |  | The show, the questions and the keys. |
| `enabled` *(required)* | `boolean` |  | Switches the bots on. |
| `count` | `number` | `24` | How many bots. |
| `seed` | `number` | `11` | Makes the crowd repeatable. |

```tsx
useLiveSimulation(live, ctx, simulate)
```

- Bots talk to the adapter directly. A real show has no use for this: real players answer from their own screens.

### useSurveys

The surveys, with `save`. useSurveyResponses gives the answers (all, or one survey's) with `submit`. usePrefs gives one person's notification preferences with `save`.

```ts
import { useSurveys, useSurveyResponses, usePrefs } from '@/contest/hooks/useContestData'
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `surveyId` | `string` |  | For `useSurveyResponses`: only this survey. |
| `participantId` | `string` |  | For `usePrefs`: whose preferences. |

```tsx
const { data: surveys = [] } = useSurveys()
const { submit } = useSurveyResponses(survey.id)
const { data: prefs, save } = usePrefs(me.id)
```

### useRankReplay

What changed since I last looked, for a ranking: it shows the ranking the person saw last time, then moves to the current one, so rows slide into their new places.

```ts
import { useRankReplay } from '@/contest/hooks/useRankReplay'
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ranked` *(required)* | `RankedRow[]` |  | The current ranking, best first. |
| `storageKey` *(required)* | `string` |  | Tells rankings apart in this browser, for example "public" and "admin". |
| `pauseMs` | `number` | `700` | How long the old ranking stays before it moves. |

```tsx
const ranked = rankParticipants(people, submissions)
const { rows, changes } = useRankReplay(ranked, 'public')
<Leaderboard rows={rows} changes={changes} />
```

- `changes` is how many places each person gained (positive) or lost since the last visit. It is undefined the first time.

### useMySubmission

One participant's own submission, created on first use, with `saveAnswer` and `submit`. Submitting locks it and scores it from the keys.

```ts
import { useMySubmission } from '@/contest/hooks/useContestData'
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `participantId` *(required)* | `string` |  | Whose submission. |

```tsx
const { data: submission, saveAnswer, submit } = useMySubmission(me.id)
```

### useContest

The remaining read hooks: the contest itself, participants, all submissions, announcements, notifications and the audit trail. Each returns `data`, `loading`, `error` and its own save calls.

```ts
import { useContest, useParticipants, useSubmissions, useAnnouncements, useNotifications, useAudit } from '@/contest/hooks/useContestData'
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `recipientId` | `string` |  | For `useNotifications`: whose notifications. |
| `pollMs` | `number` |  | For `useNotifications` (default 4000), `useAnnouncements` and `useSubmissions` (default 0, off): ask again every that many milliseconds. |

```tsx
const { data: contest } = useContest()
const { data: audit = [], revert } = useAudit()
const { data: notes = [], markRead } = useNotifications(me.id)
```

- `useAudit().revert(id, actor)` puts an entity back the way it was before that entry. The revert is a new entry with `of` set to the entry it reverted.
- `useParticipants()` also gives `invite(people)`; `useSubmissions()` gives `saveScore`; `useAnnouncements()` gives `save` and `send`.
